extracted.intended_audience: readers and writers of periodical essays / literate public interested in manners, humour, and criticism
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and exemplars for composing short, witty periodical essays and character sketches—covering comic characterisation, tone, audience-tailoring, and the critic/audience relationship. Drawn from The Spectator's model of social satire and polished prose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comic characterisation grounded in good sense
rubrics_metrics.description: His Singularities proceed from his good Sense, and are Contradictions to the Manners of the World, only as he thinks the World is in the wrong.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create eccentric or humorous characters whose oddities are rooted in reasoned conviction rather than mere caprice; such grounding makes them agreeable rather than merely ridiculous. (Example: Sir Roger's singularities arise from sensible views, which helps him please and oblige those who know him.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Humour should avoid sourness or obstinacy
rubrics_metrics.description: this Humour creates him no Enemies, for he does nothing with Sourness or Obstinacy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tone comedic observations so they aren't bitter or stubborn; amiable humour that lacks malice maintains goodwill and broad appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flexibility in fashion/style pleases
rubrics_metrics.description: being unconfined to Modes and Forms, makes him but the readier and more capable to please and oblige all who know him.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid slavish adherence to contemporary modes or rigid forms in character or manner; adaptability and disregard for transient fashions can increase a character's charm and longevity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classical learning lends authority to criticism
rubrics_metrics.description: Aristotle and Longinus are much better understood by him than Littleton or Cooke... His Familiarity with the Customs, Manners, Actions, and Writings of the Antients, makes him a very delicate Observer of what occurs to him in the present World.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A critic or commentator informed by classical models and broad reading can make subtler, more valuable judgments about plays and manners; such learned taste refines both criticism and conversation.

rubrics_metrics.name: A discerning audience/critic elevates performance
rubrics_metrics.description: It is for the Good of the Audience when he is at a Play, for the Actors have an Ambition to please him.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presence of knowledgeable, attentive spectators encourages actors and writers to improve; cultivate a readership/ audience whose taste spurs higher quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Perspicuity (clarity) is as pleasurable as wit
rubrics_metrics.description: The Perspicuity of his Discourse gives the same Pleasure that Wit would in another Man.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clear, straightforward expression can be as satisfying as cleverness; favour intelligible, lucid prose over showy erudition when aiming to please.

rubrics_metrics.name: Frankness and candid tone in conversation
rubrics_metrics.description: With this Candour does the Gentleman speak of himself and others. The same Frankness runs through all his Conversation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A tone of honest, moderate frankness—neither boastful nor obsequious—creates an agreeable voice for characters and narrators; modesty is virtuous but occasional assertiveness about one's merits may be necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specialised social knowledge enliven conversation
rubrics_metrics.description: All his Conversation and Knowledge has been in the female World... In all these important Relations, he has ever about the same Time received a kind Glance, or a Blow of a Fan, from some celebrated Beauty... This Way of Talking of his, very much enlivens the Conversation among us of a more sedate Turn.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Characters or narrators who possess deep, specific knowledge of a social sphere (fashion, courtship, etc.) can vivify dialogue and provide reliable comic material; specialization in topic can contrast and animate more sober company.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authors should write to satisfy themselves, not fame
rubrics_metrics.description: It is an endless and frivolous Pursuit to act by any other Rule than the Care of satisfying our own Minds in what we do.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritise the integrity of your design and the satisfaction of your own judgment over anxious pursuit of reputation; this produces steadier, truer work and reduces self-defeating vanity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tailor style and air to the intended audience
rubrics_metrics.description: When it is a Woman's Day, in my Works, I shall endeavour at a Stile and Air suitable to their Understanding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adapt tone, diction, and emphasis to the sensibilities of specific reader groups (e.g., women, the learned, the fashionable) rather than using a single uniform voice for all occasions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theatre (and performance) requires appropriate architecture and accessibility
rubrics_metrics.description: the house was too large, and its architecture swallowed up the voices of the actors... They contracted the width of the theatre, brought down its enormously high ceiling, thus made the words of the plays audible, and had the town to themselves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Physical and logistical conditions (size, acoustics, location, cost of access) materially affect theatrical success; in producing comic performance, ensure venue, scale, and audience access match the work's needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cultivate observation by speaking less
rubrics_metrics.description: I have indulged my Silence to such an Extravagance... the few who are intimate with me, answer my Smiles with concurrent Sentences... I have... a more than ordinary Penetration in Seeing; and flatter my self that I have looked into the Highest and Lowest of Mankind, and make shrewd Guesses...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practice restraint of speech to sharpen observation—quietness can yield richer material for humour writing and truer insight into characters and situations.
